text:
The Los Angeles Rams, Seattle Seahawks and Buffalo Bills are ranked as the top three most interesting teams to watch.

Key storylines include coaching changes, quarterback competitions and the return of star players from injury.

Now that teams have wrapped up organized team activities, workouts and minicamps, we’ve reached the dead zone of the NFL offseason.

It’s that four- to five-week stretch of nothingness where the players are allowed to get away, clubs basically turn off the office lights, and more times than not, the news cycle slows to a virtual stop.

Things won’t start getting back to normal until teams begin reporting to training camp. The Arizona Cardinals, by virtue of being selected to play in the Hall of Fame Game against the Carolina Panthers on Thursday, Aug. 6, will be among the first to get started again. They’re scheduled to report to camp on July 22 at State Farm Stadium.

If you are obsessed with the NFL, you may as well pack your bags and head out on vacation for a spell so that the silence doesn’t become too deafening. When you get back — or before you leave — you can follow our NFL Power Rankings version that suggests “The Top 32 NFL Teams to Follow” once training camp arrives:

Don’t miss this bunch

1. Los Angeles Rams

They’re the Super Bowl favorites and they have the league’s reigning Most Valuable Player in ageless quarterback Matthew Stafford and the defending Defensive Player of the Year now that they’ve traded for edge rusher extraordinaire Myles Garrett. A team coached by Sean McVay is always fun to watch, but the Rams always make for good headlines, too, and they’ll give you your fill.

2. Seattle Seahawks

The defending champions might not seem as sexy a story as their NFC West rivals in Los Angeles, but don’t expect them to operate under the radar. The Seahawks know how to stir up the noise and excitement and when the franchise finally gets sold to new ownership, watch out.

3. Buffalo Bills

The pressure is on Joe Brady now that he’s been chosen to replace Sean McDermott as coach, and the clock is about to start on whether he can do what McDermott could not and finally help deliver a Super Bowl title to folks in Buffalo. QB Josh Allen moves to the hot seat as well, in a slightly different way. Get ready for a healthy dose of crazy atmosphere at new Highmark Stadium.

4. New England Patriots

We shall see if coach Mike Vrabel is able to navigate his way out of some unsavory and unflattering media scrutiny or if the drama implodes. The Patriots have a lot going for themselves after making it to the Super Bowl this past season, namely quarterback Drake Maye and the arrival of a No. 1 wide receiver in A.J. Brown.

5. Chicago Bears

Millions of eyes are going to be on this franchise as it creeps closer and closer to becoming a Super Bowl contender. Maybe this is the year. The Bears have the weapons and the smarts to make it happen if they don’t get complacent or distracted by their success.

6. Baltimore Ravens

They’ve got a new head coach and a new offensive coordinator, but the Ravens remain a formidable team that will compete and create havoc in the AFC North. The quicker the players can replicate all of the new doctrines and execute the plans, the better they will start the season.

7. Kansas City Chiefs

This bunch might seem like its best days are behind them and the dynasty is dying, but don’t sleep on the Chiefs. Andy Reid is still the coach. Patrick Mahomes is still the quarterback, although he’s returning from a torn ACL. They also recently gave him a record contract extension, which should tell you something. Check in on these guys once camp begins and be happy you did.

8. Detroit Lions

Two big things to follow here will be the health of the Lions’ defense, which was decimated the past couple of seasons, and how fast new offensive coordinator Drew Petzing (formerly of the Cardinals) can get Jared Goff and Co. moving at high-speed velocity. Everything figures to begin with dynamo running back Jahmyr Gibbs, but we’ve got to see all of it develop.

9. Philadelphia Eagles

I'm going to be a little bit more than curious to see if the Eagles, who have become somewhat of an NFL enigma, can find their way. New OC Sean Mannion must fit a new type of system around QB Jalen Hurts, and it’s fair to wonder how Hurts will respond while operating mostly under center. Saquon Barkley might find it desirable as the feature running back, but who really knows where this team is headed in 2026?

10. Los Angeles Chargers

Back-to-back 11-win years show real promise under third-year coach Jim Harbaugh, but will the Chargers become more than just postseason wild-card fodder for the rest of the AFC? The jury might be out, but the thinking here is that they can, and they just might. But again, tune into their training camp activities to learn more.

11. Dallas Cowboys

We can never be sure what we’re about to witness and learn from the Cowboys once they huddle into the supposed secrecy of training camp, which usually is anything but secret. There are going to be stories and drama, though, and you just feel it coming. That’s OK, though. It’s the Cowboys’ way.

12. Cincinnati Bengals

Upon adding Dexter Lawrence to bolster their defensive front, it now feels as if it’s up to quarterback Joe Burrow and his two ace receivers to take the Bengals to the next level. Will they get there? There’s a good chance, yes. But Cincinnati needs a steady and boring training camp without any needless bad PR to get there.

13. Denver Broncos

Fans will need to see steady progress and improved health from young quarterback Bo Nix after he suffered a fractured right ankle in the AFC divisional playoffs. The sooner he can get back into some sort of rhythm, the sooner Denver can see what it can do with its new weapon at wideout, Jaylen Waddle, who comes over from the Dolphins.

14. Houston Texans

The biggest thing to monitor here is how the Texans’ offense can get back off the ground behind quarterback C.J. Stroud and a running game that’s been grounded. Coach DeMeco Ryan’s defense should be just as scary as ever, but Houston must find a way to score points, grab a lead and let its defense cook. It all starts in camp.

15. Green Bay Packers

When will All-World edge rusher Micah Parsons return from his torn ACL? The latest estimates aren’t until sometime in mid-October, at best, so that’s where the news will be. While the watch party commences on Parsons, keep an eye on how quarterback Jordan Love can regenerate his connection with wideouts Christian Watson and Matthew Golden.

Still plenty to see here

16. Minnesota Vikings

Just being able to spy a little bit on the supposed quarterback competition between newcomer Kyler Murray (the former No. 1 overall pick by the Cardinals) and the Vikings’ own former first-round pick, J.J. McCarthy, will be worth its weight in gold. Whoever most pleases top wide receiver Justin Jefferson is sure to be named the winner by coach Kevin O’Connell, assuming he doesn’t already have a favorite.

17. Jacksonville Jaguars

It can be easy not to get overwhelmed by the Jaguars’ roster, which is why we’ve got Jacksonville in this spot, actually. But there is a growing sense that somehow, the magic might return under coach Liam Coen. We shall see. I’m not so sure.

18. San Francisco 49ers

How much of a difference will the addition of veteran wide receiver Mike Evans bring to an already competent offense led by coach Kyle Shanahan? Evans will be among the top players to watch when the 49ers report to camp, and this team is in desperate need of good health, less drama and more good vibes.

19. Indianapolis Colts

The news will and should be focused on the health of quarterback Daniel Jones, who is on the mend from a torn Achilles and became one of the league’s great reclamation stories before getting hurt. I’m also just as curious to see how much stud running back Jonathan Taylor has left in that gifted career.

20. Pittsburgh Steelers

It feels as if the Steelers might be headed for a fall in 2026. Mike Tomlin walked away and Mike McCarthy is in as coach, where he reunites with Aaron Rodgers, 42. Their days in Green Bay were a long time ago. Pittsburgh’s defense will keep the Steelers in games, but it will be interesting to see how the offense rolls once camp gets underway.

21. New Orleans Saints

There’s a lot to like about this team, starting at quarterback with former Chandler Hamilton standout Tyler Shough. The additions of guard David Anderson, running back Travis Etienne Jr. and rookie receiver Jordyn Tyson should make things that much more special. Coach Kellen Moore must keep the momentum going when camp hits.

22. New York Giants

Some skeptics will overlook some of the Giants’ shortcomings because of the arrival of coach John Harbaugh. What’s more realistic is seeing how Harbaugh decides to proceed with quarterback Jaxson Dart and whether he curtails some of Dart’s free-wheeling style — and if he can develop a more balanced offense.

23. Las Vegas Raiders

They won’t be expected to win many games, but how will the Raiders handle veteran QB Kirk Cousins and rookie Fernando Mendoza, the No. 1 overall pick? The quarterback situation alone will be worth watching once the team reassembles.

24. Tampa Bay Buccaneers

Don’t wait for training camp to get the latest on the Buccaneers, especially as it relates to quarterback Baker Mayfield and the contract extension everyone involved seems to want but can’t get done. Mayfield said he won’t negotiate once camp begins, so it’s now or never — at least until the franchise tag comes into play.

25. Tennessee Titans

Is Cam Ward ready to take a leap in Year 2? It might happen with new coach Robert Saleh bringing in offensive guru Brian Daboll to help. The Titans stocked up during free agency and significantly improved a good portion of their roster. Keep your eyes on Ward’s ongoing chemistry with new receivers Wan’Dale Robinson (from the Giants) and Carnell Tate (the fourth overall pick).

26. Washington Commanders

It’s too early to tell just who the Commanders are. They should be better than the club that finished 5-12 a year ago, mostly because of injuries. But they hardly look like potential NFC champions, which they were just two seasons ago. Let’s see how quarterback Jayden Daniels responds with new coordinator David Blough. Kliff Kingsbury left and is now the assistant head coach of the Rams.

27. Carolina Panthers

Somebody had to win the NFC South last season and these guys managed to do it by owning a tiebreaker over the Buccaneers and Falcons. The Panthers did bolster a decent defense by adding pass rusher Jaelan Phillips and linebacker Devin Lloyd, but is there a way they can get more out of Bryce Young and the offense?

Watch at your own risk

28. Miami Dolphins

The Dolphins might not be as boring as some expect. They probably will be bad, yes, but a backfield with Malik Willis and De’Von Achane could have its moments of electricity. If a pass catcher or two can step up their game, maybe they’ll surprise folks. The defense is another story, though.

29. Atlanta Falcons

Storylines to follow include the QB competition between Michael Penix Jr. and Tua Tagovailoa, outside linebacker James Pearce Jr.’s legal issues and how coach Kevin Stefanski can try to help further elevate running back Bijan Robinson’s game.

30. Arizona Cardinals

Who’s going to emerge as the starting quarterback and will it even matter? At some point, rookie Carson Beck is going to get his shot and by then, the season might already be heading toward a disaster. Stay tuned to learn how rookie Jeremiyah Love and the running backs will split time, how the defense hopes to rediscover itself and how first-year coach Mike LaFleur plans to get things off the ground.

31. New York Jets

Despite some very decent roster upgrades in the offseason, the Jets are still the Jets in that they still don’t have a new franchise quarterback and don’t have enough star power elsewhere to lead them back to respectability. Maybe training camp will offer some good news, but don’t bet on it.

32. Cleveland Browns

There’s no buzz left around this bunch now that Myles Garrett has been traded to the Rams. The star edge rusher was the last shiny piece holding this thing together, and now it just looks like a hopeless endeavor. Coach Todd Monken has his hands full, and it will be interesting to see how fans react if Deshaun Watson is allowed to become the starting quarterback.

Langford had only recently worked his way back from a lengthy absence after missing more than a month with a right forearm strain. Since returning to the lineup earlier this month, the young outfielder quickly regained his offensive rhythm and became one of Texas' most dangerous bats.

Over his last 20 games, Langford hit .317 with seven home runs while consistently producing in the middle of the Rangers' lineup.

He also reached base in each of his previous 10 games and was hitting .390 across his last 14 plate appearances. His strong run elevated his season batting average to .278 while pushing his OPS to a season-best .824.

Unfortunately for both Langford and the Rangers, injuries have continued to interrupt his career. This latest setback marks his sixth trip to the injured list since making his major-league debut.

He also dealt with multiple oblique injuries during the 2025 season after previously missing time with a hamstring injury during his rookie campaign.

Taking Langford's place on the active roster is outfielder Evan Carter, who has been activated from the IL after recovering from a right oblique strain.

Carter had been sidelined since suffering the injury while making a diving catch against the Boston Red Sox on June 12. Before returning, he appeared in one rehab game with Double-A Frisco, where he reached base three times by going 2-for-2 with a home run and a walk.

Although Carter has struggled offensively this season, batting .176 with six home runs and 21 RBIs in 66 games, he has remained a valuable contributor on the bases, successfully converting all 10 of his stolen-base attempts.

text:
The Cincinnati Bengals have one of the best sets of weapons around a quarterback in the NFL.

Some would argue Joe Burrow has the best. Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are perhaps the only pair of No. 1 wideouts on one team.

But the falloff after those two names is pretty steep. There’s no reliable third wideout. Running back Chase Brown hasn’t really received a major workhorse load. Tight end is a mix of slot receivers and blockers.

This explains why ESPN’s Bill Barnwell ranks the Bengals’ cast of weapons third overall behind the Los Angeles Rams and Detroit Lions.

But Barnwell also cautions that one name could lift the Bengals to the top spot: Erick All.

“After those three, well, good luck,” Barnwell wrote. “Andrei Iosivas has been one of the least efficient receivers in the league, even when one of the players ahead of him has been absent. Tight end Mike Gesicki wasn't able to build on his resurgent 2024 campaign. Erick All Jr. quietly impressed early in his rookie season before missing the second half of 2024 and all of 2025 with a serious knee injury. Could the 25-year-old tight end be the player the Bengals need to make it to No. 1 on this list?”

All, a fourth-round pick in 2024, arrived with big hype as a value who fell due to injury. He helped the Bengals offense become far more dynamic as a rookie over nine games, then suffered an injury that ended his season and cost him 2025 after complications.

If All can shake free of the injury bug, he’s a dynamic weapon for Burrow to utilize all over formations. And he’s the type of third option that would indeed help push the group up rankings like this.

In time, perhaps rookie wideout Colbie Young can be that, too. But right now, there’s a pretty big spotlight on whether All can get back and make an impact.

The Boston Red Sox have a decision to make as one of the team's interesting pitchers nears a return from injury.

After the 2024 season, the Red Sox signed six-year Los Angeles Angels veteran pitcher Patrick Sandoval to a two-year, $18 million contract. Unfortunately, a slew of injuries has sidelined the 29-year-old since 2024, but Sandoval began a rehab assignment in the minor leagues earlier this month.

Sandoval has made five minor league starts since starting his rehab assignment at the beginning of June. With MLB rules dictating that a player can only remain on a rehab assignment for a maximum of 30 days, the Red Sox will have to decide whether to activate Sandoval soon.

MassLive's Chris Cotillo believes that even when the Red Sox call up Sandoval, his role will be unclear, especially with how well Boston's starting rotation has been performing recently.

"More than two years since his last major league start, Patrick Sandoval is nearing the end of his long road back to the mound," Cotillo wrote on Sunday. "His impending return will lead to some interesting decisions for the Red Sox. When Sandoval does return, his fit in Boston’s rolling rotation is unclear. Sandoval is out of minor league options, so the Red Sox can’t send him to Worcester after his rehab clock is up.

"It’s unlikely Bennett -- who owns a 2.78 ERA in 22 ⅔ innings since being recalled -- is removed from the rotation to accommodate Sandoval. A more likely scenario involves the Red Sox either using Sandoval as a multi-inning long reliever or temporarily moving to a six-man rotation in the week before the All-Star break."

Sandoval has plenty of success in the big leagues and has been a starter for the majority of his career, yet it's hard to see how the 29-year-old could crack Boston's rotation unless the team elected to move forward with a six-man rotation.

The veteran hurler has not pitched in a major league game since 2024, so easing him in by using him out of the bullpen could be the Red Sox's best option.
